subject: Re: Kickoff: DEN for small-data tabular classification
body:
Status.

Reproduction: done April 16 via the simulation entry point; our numbers match the paper's synthetic-study results within noise.

Benchmarks so far, on 9 internal small-data tasks (120-800 labeled rows each): DEN beats gradient-boosted trees on 6 of 9, with the biggest wins exactly where the theory predicts -- tasks whose feature spaces differ most from anything in pre-training, since only the covariate transformation block needs fine-tuning and it has few parameters to overfit.

The honest caveat: on the 3 losses, the culprit is Umar's diagnosis that our synthetic pre-training task distribution undercovers heavy-tailed numeric features. He has a revised task synthesizer running; preliminary signs are good but it costs a full pre-training cycle to verify, about 9 days on our current allotment.

May 22 benchmark milestone likely slips a week. Flagging now.

Farah
